recentItems.title: Hundreds expected at Ukraine–Belarus border as humanitarian convoy arrives
recentItems.description:

Al Jazeera's Audrey MacAlpine has the latest updates.

recentItems.title: Does the death penalty deter drug crimes? Lessons from Singapore and Malaysia | 101 East Documentary
recentItems.description:
Malaysia's decision to repeal the mandatory death penalty in 2023 has led to the re-sentencing of more than 700 drug offenders, who were once condemned to hang.

The country is now considering further reform to its drug policy.

Meanwhile, the number of executions for drug trafficking in neighbouring Singapore has accelerated in recent years.

101 East follows the stories of two death row inmates, one in Malaysia and one in Singapore, to find out how the diverging approaches have impacted their families, and asks if strict laws deter drug crimes.

recentItems.description:

Al Jazeera's Richard Gaisford reports from Michigan.

recentItems.title: RSF Major General Siddiq Ander defects, says group serves Hemedti’s family project
recentItems.description:
Major General Siddiq Abdel Rahman Ander says he joined the war believing he was fighting for a united Sudan. Now he is breaking with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and urging others to do the same.

Ander headed RSF unit Group 15 and led the Sudan Liberation Forces for Reform and Development. In an exclusive video obtained by Al Jazeera English, he announces his withdrawal from the RSF and Tasees Alliance. He says it became clear they were serving a family-based project controlled by Hemedti’s relatives.

His departure comes amid other defections, including Sudan Shield Forces commander Abu Aqla Keikal in October 2024, Major General Al-Nour Ahmad Adam in April and Brigadier General Ali Rizgallah in May. Mohammad Azrag Al-Fanjari said he defected with nearly 300 fighters and 30 vehicles. The total number is unclear.

Al Jazeera’s Al-Miqdad Al-Ruhaid reports from Khartoum, Sudan.

recentItems.title: Joint Russia-Ukraine convoy leaves occupied Oleshky to evacuate up to 750 civilians
recentItems.description:
A humanitarian convoy to evacuate as many as 750 civilians has left the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in Ukraine.

Oleshky has been under Russian control since the first days of the invasion in February 2022. Thousands have been trapped there, and many have reported eating garden weeds to survive.

Evacuated residents were given the choice to leave Russian-occupied territory and return to Ukraine through Belarus, or to resettle in Russia. The operation is also bringing food, medicine, fuel and other supplies.

Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets says joint aid will be delivered to all residents who remain in Oleshky, and help given to those leaving for Ukraine or Russia. Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova thanked her counterpart for ensuring the ceasefire was maintained.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says this is an isolated humanitarian arrangement coordinated with the US, and not a sign of any breakthrough in peace negotiations. 

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine in Kyiv and Yulia Shapovalova in Moscow report.
